[[File:Lwowscy_matematycy1930.jpg | thumb | right | alt=Lviv mathematicians, 1930. | Lviv mathematicians, 1930.]]The '''Polish School of Mathematics''' was the [[mathematics]] community that flourished in [[Poland]] in the 20th century, particularly during the [[Interbellum]] between [[World War I|World Wars I]] and [[World War II|II]].

== Overview ==
The Polish School of Mathematics subsumed:

*the [[Lwów School of Mathematics]] - mostly focused on [[functional analysis]];
*the [[Warsaw School of Mathematics]] - mostly focused on [[set theory]], [[mathematical logic]] and [[topology]]; and
*the [[Kraków School of Mathematics]] - mostly focused on [[differential equations]], [[analytic functions]], [[differential geometry]].

=== Nomenclature ===
Poland's mathematicians provided a name to [[Polish notation]] and [[Polish space]].

=== Background ===
It has been debated what stimulated the exceptional efflorescence of mathematics in Poland after [[World War I]].  Important preparatory work had been done by the [[Positivism in Poland|Polish "Positivists"]] following the disastrous [[January Uprising|January 1863 Uprising]].  The Positivists extolled [[science]] and [[technology]], and popularized slogans of "organic work" and "building from the foundations."  In the 20th century, mathematics was a field of endeavor that could be successfully pursued even with the limited resources that Poland commanded in the [[interbellum]] period.

=== Historical Influences ===
Over the centuries, Polish mathematicians have influenced the course of history.  [[Copernicus]] used mathematics to buttress his revolutionary [[heliocentric theory]].  Four hundred years later, [[Marian Rejewski]] — subsequently assisted by fellow [[mathematician]]-[[cryptologist]]s [[Jerzy Różycki]] and [[Henryk Zygalski]] — in December 1932 first broke the German [[Enigma machine]] [[cipher]], thus laying the foundations for [[Great Britain|British]] [[World War II]] reading of Enigma ciphers ("[[Ultra (cryptography)|Ultra]]").  After the war, [[Stanisław Ulam]] showed [[Edward Teller]] how to construct a practicable [[hydrogen bomb]].
